title: Level-adjusted ROM by degeneration grade, statistical-model estimates (Kettler 2011)

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: general-linear-model mean estimate of full-range ROM adjusted for spinal level (NZ FE/LB back-transformed from log), with 95% CI

source.authors: Kettler A, Rohlmann F, Ring C, Mack C, Wilke HJ
source.sample: 203 human lumbar segments (L1-L2 to L4-L5; mono- and polysegmental specimens, up to 4 discs) from 111 donors in the Ulm in vitro database; radiographic degeneration grade 0-3 (Wilke system)
source.age: donors 18-99 y (Table 1; text 19-99), median 56, mean 55.9 ± 15.2 (known for 107)

protocol.summary: Ulm database: pure moments ±7.5 Nm without axial preload, five uncontrolled DOF unconstrained, same spine tester; third loading cycle evaluated. ROM = rotation between +7.5 and -7.5 Nm (full range); NZ = laxity at 0 Nm. Levels L1-L2..L4-L5 pooled (L5-S1 excluded). Rate not stated (Ulm standard, Wilke 1998).
how_to_simulate: Fix the caudal vertebra; leave the cranial end free; no preload
Apply ±7.5 Nm pure moments in flexion/extension, left/right lateral bending, left/right axial rotation (3 cycles, evaluate the 3rd)
Report full-range ROM (+7.5 to -7.5 Nm) and NZ for each plane; compare per degeneration grade (grade 0 = no degeneration)
Pooled over L1-L2..L4-L5: compare a level-averaged model or the level of interest with care
protocol.notes: ROM and NZ are sums of both directions (flex+ext, left+right). Original data = mean ± SD of all levels pooled (Figs 2-4 left); model estimates = level-adjusted general-linear-model means with 95% CI (Figs 2-4 right, Tables 3-4).

extraction.from: Results text (grade 0 and 3 values) + Table 3 (increase vs grade 0) for grades 1-2; 95% CIs digitised from Figs 2-4 right panels
extraction.uncertainty: means: text/Table 3 values (0.1 deg rounding; grades 1-2 = grade-0 value + Table 3 increment); AR ROM grade 0 not in text - 3.9 digitised (whisker midpoint 3.89) and grades 1-3 = 3.9 + Table 3 increments; CIs ±0.1 deg digitised; AR NZ CI lower ends for grades 1-2 not resolvable
extraction.check_notes: Digitised bar tops (+0.1 deg outline offset) reproduce 9.5/8.9/8.3/6.4 FE and 10.2/8.8/8.2/6.8 LB; AR NZ bars digitise ~0.40/0.42/0.47/0.47 vs 0.4/0.5/0.6/0.6 from Table 3 increments (rounding of a 0.4 base) - AR NZ model values uncertain ±0.1. FE NZ grade 3: text gives 1.3 (used) whereas grade 0 + Table 3 increment gives 1.2 (back-transformation rounding).

shared_sample_with: wilke2025: Ulm database; Wilke 2025 pools the same institutional data (largely overlapping specimens)
heuer2007a/heuer2008: Ulm specimens of 2005-2008 likely included (not itemised)
